text: In multi-scale modeling of biological systems, properties of the whole system that cannot be predicted from its individual components alone -- such as cell-cycle timing arising from interacting oscillators and checkpoints -- are called ___ properties.
explanation: Emergent properties arise from the interactions among a system's components rather than from any single component in isolation -- examples include cell cycle timing (from interacting oscillators and checkpoints), cell polarity (from Turing-like mechanisms), and bet-hedging phenotypic diversity (from stochastic switching). Whole-cell and multi-scale models are specifically valuable because they provide a rigorous, mechanistic way to study how such emergent behaviors arise from lower-level interactions.
